topSignals.title: Mizuho upgrades Bloom Energy to Outperform ($242 PT, 48% upside); FCEL surges 29% as sector re-rates
topSignals.text: — On July 30, Mizuho analyst Maheep Mandloi flipped from Neutral to Outperform with a $242 price target — 48% upside from the ~$163 July 29 close. Rationale: faster-than-expected operating leverage, $27B+ in financing capacity, all major US hyperscalers validated, backlog growing faster than revenue. FCEL rose 29% to $23.06 as a sector sympathy play on no FCEL-specific news. The Mizuho upgrade is the most significant rating action since the Q2 blowout and reinforces the "cheap valuation after pullback" thesis. Mizuho upgrade — MarketScreener | 24/7 Wall St.

topSignals.title: BE retreats to $159.80 midday July 31 — post-earnings profit-taking structural despite upgrade catalyst
topSignals.text: — Despite Mizuho's upgrade and a +26-28% intraday surge on July 30, BE is trading at $159.80 (−4.22%, −$7.04) on July 31. Full pattern since Q2 earnings (July 28 close): $184.89 → +11% AH → ~$164 July 29 close → ~$160 early July 30 → +26-28% intraday on Mizuho upgrade → back below $167 close → $159.80 July 31. All 27 analyst price targets (range $242–$350) remain above the current trading price. The persistent sell-off implies structural profit-taking by holders of the +1,300% YTD run. TipRanks July 30 | Yahoo Finance BE

topSignals.title: FERC RM26-4: ISO-NE abeyance deadline August 3 (3 days) — binary trigger for non-ERCOT LCOE modeling
topSignals.text: — ISO-NE must submit its abeyance request by August 3, three days from now. If granted: ISO-NE (and by precedent MISO, PJM, CAISO) gets until November 16 to propose tariff reform, delaying modelable avoided-transmission-cost ($5-20/MWh) inputs for non-Texas SOFC LCOE scenarios. If denied: August 17 hard deadline for all RTOs forces immediate reform filings and opens the path to modeling the non-ERCOT avoided-T-cost benefit within weeks. This is the highest-impact near-term policy binary for the LCOE model. FERC RM26-4 | Day Pitney analysis

items.text: Elcogen: No new announcements July 31. EFCF 2026 proceedings embargo now day 28+ (exceeds typical 2-3 week post-conference window by over one week); papers are almost certainly in journal peer review. ELCO I factory (Tallinn, 360 MW/yr) in ongoing volume production; E3000 G2 deliveries continuing. Status: watch elcogen.com for embargo lift.

Topsoe: No new SOFC/SOEC announcements July 31. Herning SOEC factory (500 MW/yr) remains hibernated. Recent Topsoe news cycle: $1.6B Jordan green ammonia FEED (July 14), Sasol eSAF licensing (July 14). SOFC data-center pathway deferred to 2029+ per H2 access constraints. No change.

Bloom Energy Q2 transcript — shipped MW analyst estimate: Analyst parsing of the Q2 call indicates H2 2026 shipments of approximately 606-716 MW per quarter. If accurate, full-year 2026 shipped MW would reach approximately 1.2-1.4 GW (implying a current run-rate below the 2 GW/yr Fremont nameplate — consistent with BE's statement that it is "on track for 2 GW annual production capacity by end of 2026," i.e., the ramp is still in progress). This analyst estimate is not confirmed by an explicit MW disclosure in the transcript. Utility Dive

Project Jupiter (New Mexico, 2.45 GW): No new July 31 developments. Status unchanged: NM AG criminal investigation into fraudulent public comments ongoing; July 28 county meeting resulted in demonstrator arrests; Oracle $4.7B economic impact PR ongoing; air permit hearing October 19 (Sunland Park Multi-Generational Center); gas pipeline dead-end (two NM Land Commissioner rejections). SemiAnalysis 2029 first-power base case unchanged.

Background pipeline (unchanged): Crusoe/Tallgrass Cheyenne 900 MW Phase 1 (Bloom, H2 2026 target), FCEL/Fit Energy 380 MW total (30 MW funded), Equinix 100+ MW, AEP/Bloom Wyoming 1 GW (2030), Bloom/Brookfield $25B framework, Quanta Computer $502M islanded microgrid (3 AI-server plants, Fremont CA). No new deployments announced July 31.

FERC RM26-4 — 3 days to ISO-NE abeyance deadline: See Top Signal #3. ISO-NE must file abeyance request by August 3. Outcome shapes whether PJM, MISO, CAISO, and ISO-NE avoided-transmission-cost can be modeled in the SOFC LCOE within the coming months. FERC RM26-4

New York moratorium threshold correction — 50 MW, not 20 MW: Review of the executive order language confirms the NY data center moratorium applies to new facilities of 50 MW or larger (not 20 MW — that threshold is FERC's large-load definition in RM26-4). Facilities below 50 MW and on-site islanded generation (SOFC's key differentiator) are not covered by the state permit ban. Prior digest notation corrected. Mondaq practical analysis | CNBC

New York: Hochul signals nuclear ambition, awaiting federal go-ahead: In the context of the moratorium, Governor Hochul stated she is waiting for the Trump administration's approval to roll out a New York nuclear energy plan. No specifics or timeline given. Structural position unchanged: no new NY nuclear capacity before 2030+; SOFC's 90-day deployment advantage intact in NY. Readtangle
Quiet day. Background benchmarks unchanged: CCGT $2,000-2,200/kW capex, SMRs 2030+, solar+storage $25/MWh LCOE (unsuitable for 24/7 baseload AI workloads).

Bloom Energy (BE): $159.80 (−4.22%, −$7.04) midday July 31. July 30 Mizuho upgrade (Neutral → Outperform, $242 PT) triggered a +26-28% intraday surge on July 30; stock closed July 30 session ~$166 before continuing lower to $159.80 on July 31. Full analyst PT landscape: Mizuho $242 (new Outperform), Clear Street $290 (Buy, July 28), UBS $300 (raised from $350, July 30), prior consensus avg. ~$280-286 (27 analysts: 8 Strong Buy, 2 Moderate Buy, 16 Hold, 1 Strong Sell). All PTs above current $159.80. 24/7 Wall St. | TipRanks | MarketScreener Mizuho

FuelCell Energy (FCEL): $23.06 on July 30 (+29% sympathy rally); YTD +212%. Analyst consensus PT $22.83 (slightly below the July 30 close). No company-specific catalyst for the July 30 move — pure sector re-rating on Bloom's Q2 blowout. Next FCEL catalyst: Q3 FY2026 earnings (October). ts2.tech
Ceres Power (LON: CWR): No new news. ~−40% MTD. H1 2026 results (September) remain next scheduled catalyst.

New PMC publication — creep damage SOFC (PMC12942563, 2026): "Material Composition Design for Long-Term Stability of Solid Oxide Fuel Cell Based on Creep Damage and Failure Probability" — newly indexed on PubMed Central. Models SOFC operation at 50,000 h (5.7 years) under high-temperature creep conditions; evaluates anode/cathode/electrolyte composition effects on failure probability. Cell/materials focus, but the 50,000 h lifetime modelling framework is relevant to stack replacement interval assumptions in system LCOE models. PMC

Advanced Science air-supply degradation paper (advs.202516807): Now formally indexed on PubMed Central (PMC12806198), confirming full journal publication in Advanced Science Vol. 13, 2026. Previously flagged July 30. PMC

Quiet day. No new system-level SOFC TEA/LCOE papers identified July 31. The creep damage paper above is cell-level, not system TEA. Prior active references unchanged: EPFL Nat. Commun. 17:2421 (66.3% system efficiency / 0.2%/kh degradation), RSC Green Chemistry UK CHP TEA (H2-fed 92.12% system efficiency), SOFC-GT-SE multi-objective optimization (Energy 345, 2026).

lcoe.text: BE H2 2026 shipment analyst estimate — 606-716 MW/quarter: At Q2 product revenue of $935.4M and ~600 MW shipped (midpoint), implied realized revenue ~$1,558/kW. With 33.4% gross margin → manufacturing cost proxy ~$1,038/kW for direct product (caution: revenue mix may include EaaS/service recognition inflating ASP). Treat as directional only — base capex update deferred until explicit shipped MW disclosure.

FERC RM26-4 August 3 abeyance outcome (72 hours): Schedule a model update pass for August 4. If abeyance denied: incorporate $5-20/MWh avoided-T-cost as a live input for PJM/MISO/CAISO/ISO-NE scenarios. If granted: leave those inputs as placeholders pending November 16 stakeholder process.

NY moratorium threshold correction (50 MW, not 20 MW): Revise NY market sizing in LCOE pipeline model. SOFC deployments serving data center loads below 50 MW (edge compute, modular micro-DC, small AI inference nodes) are unaffected even for grid-connected configurations. Deployments ≥50 MW that are fully islanded may also be outside the moratorium's permit trigger.

BE market-implied cost of capital: $159.80 with all 27 analyst PTs at $242-350 implies deep discount — driven by profit-taking, not fundamental doubts. Structural: keep WACC sensitivity band at 10.5-11% (not 9-10%) in the LCOE model until BE stabilizes above $180.

Creep damage paper (PMC12942563): If the 50,000 h failure probability curves in this paper show material composition-dependent degradation significantly above 15-year targets at operating temperature, add a "high-degradation stack" scenario to the LCOE model. Stack replacement at 10-12 years (vs. 15-year base) increases LCOE by 15-25%.
